mainEntity.name: What is steel-stud framing and where is it typically used?

acceptedAnswer.text: Steel-stud framing uses cold-formed, galvanized steel tracks and studs instead of traditional lumber to build walls, partitions, and ceilings. It is non-combustible, perfectly straight, and resistant to termites, rot, and moisture damage. Light-gauge steel is widely used for interior commercial partition walls, while heavy-gauge structural steel handles load-bearing exterior framing. Unlike wood, steel will not warp, twist, or shrink over time, which prevents drywall popping and nail pops down the line. It creates a dimensionally stable framework that works well for both commercial buildouts and modern residential interiors.
